name: Quebec
summary: A white cross on blue with a white fleur-de-lis in each quarter. Adopted in 1948 by Premier Maurice Duplessis, it recalls the French royal heritage of New France.
origin: The design developed from the Carillon flag, a 19th-century banner linked to the French victory at Fort Carillon in 1758. Nationalists in the early 20th century promoted a version with a cross and fleurs-de-lis.
Premier Maurice Duplessis's government adopted the Fleurdelisé by order in council on 21 January 1948, now Quebec Flag Day, replacing the Union Flag over the National Assembly.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: From French royal banners and the heavens.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The cross and lilies; from the royal white of France.

symbols.name: White cross
symbols.meaning: Christianity and the French royal naval ensign of New France.

symbols.name: Four fleurs-de-lis
symbols.description: White lilies pointing upward in each quarter.
symbols.meaning: The French monarchy and Quebec's French origins.

history.label: Carillon-Sacré-Cœur flag
history.note: Used by nationalists; fleurs-de-lis pointed to the centre.

facts: The fleurs-de-lis point upward; on the earlier Carillon flag they pointed toward the centre.
clues: A white cross on blue with four white fleurs-de-lis.
Its lilies recall a French royal heritage in North America.
Adopted in 1948 to replace the Union Flag over a provincial assembly.
